CMP-13.title: Separating within-trial from across-trial component effect modification
CMP-13.question: Component ML-NMR fits one shared interaction on a globally centered covariate, which algebraically forces the causal within-trial interaction to equal the confounded across-trial association. How much does that cost, when, and is the damage really caused by aggregate data as the catalog claims?
CMP-13.answer: Fitting one shared interaction matrix on a globally centered covariate is not pooling: for a binary modifier with study prevalence p_s it is algebraically identical to imposing that the causal within-trial coefficient equals the confounded across-trial one. In the model simulated, coverage of a nominal 95% interval for the causal interaction falls from 93.8% when that happens to be true to 17.2% when the two are equal and opposite, and further in networks whose contrasts move two components at once. Separating them costs about 5% in interval width and removes an order of magnitude of bias. The catalog's stated cause is incomplete: the loss is present with all twelve trials supplying individual data, so aggregate data are not necessary for it, but removing individual data roughly doubles the bias, so they amplify it.
findings: Coverage under the shared restriction degrades monotonically with the discordance between the within-trial and across-trial coefficients, from 93.8% at no discordance to 17.2% when they are equal and opposite, and it is worse in bundled component networks whose contrasts move two components at once than where every contrast isolates one.
Both separated estimators are nominal at every discordance examined, 92.6% to 96.3%, including under a nonlinear across-trial pattern where the linear split model is itself misspecified.

CMP-13 says aggregate studies cause the pull. With all twelve trials supplying individual patient data the shared model still has median absolute standardized bias 0.15 and coverage as low as 44.6%, so aggregate data are not necessary. But bias rises to 0.29 and coverage falls to 17.2% as individual data are removed, so they amplify it. The registered refutation threshold was narrowly missed (47% of cells against 50%) and we report that rather than moving it.

Where a component appears in no individual-data arm, the three methods behave in three different ways: the IPD-anchored estimator declines to report it in 100% of replicates; the shared model returns a confident -0.34 against a truth of zero, sourced entirely from the across-trial gradient; and the joint split returns intervals so wide that coverage approaches one, when it returns one at all.

A study-clustered sandwich, included so the comparison could not be won on the variance estimator, covered 75.4% to 92.4% where the shared model is correctly specified. With twelve clusters it is badly anticonservative, and it is reported as a finding rather than used as the comparator.
CMP-13.not_answered: The registered global analysis is uninformative and the regime split that produced a usable answer was prompted by observing that failure, so it is not prespecified. The general headline about component ML-NMR is not established: the likelihood and nuisance structures are not mapped onto the fixed- and random-effect specifications the implemented method offers, and free study-by-treatment effects or priors can absorb or alter the term the identity isolates. A maximum-likelihood analogue of component ML-NMR. Implemented ML-NMR is Bayesian and priors matter most where interactions are weakly identified, so the coverage numbers do not transfer to multinma; the algebra does, and therefore so does the direction. One binary modifier, a log link, a Poisson outcome, additive components with no synergy, no random treatment-effect heterogeneity, no inconsistency, and exactly reported study prevalences. Under the discordance patterns the split model is correctly specified, so the study measures the cost of an algebraically known restriction rather than establishing that real networks contain within/across disagreement or how large it typically is. Continuous or multiple correlated modifiers, misspecified aggregate covariate distributions, and time-to-event outcomes are untested. It does not touch IDN-05.
CMP-13.design: Twelve-trial two-component Poisson network with a binary effect modifier whose prevalence varies across studies, aggregate arms generated by exact integration. 320 scenarios crossing network structure, the discordance between within-trial and across-trial modification, IPD availability including a case where one component has no within-trial data at all, arm size and prevalence spread. 2000 replicates each.
CMP-13.estimand: Within-trial component interaction on the conditional log-rate scale

CMU-02.title: Do prior-sensitivity diagnostics catch the analyses that are actually wrong?
CMU-02.question: In a population-adjusted network a proper prior yields a proper posterior even where the likelihood identifies nothing, so a narrow interval can reflect the prior rather than the evidence. The diagnostics that would expose this exist. What are their operating characteristics: do they flag the analyses whose intervals actually miss the truth, and how often do they cry wolf?
CMU-02.answer: At the thresholds the literature suggests, they miss most of it. Pairing each warning with whether that replicate's own interval missed, a composite of four diagnostics has sensitivity 0.37 at a false-alarm rate of 0.16, falling to 0.13 outside two engineered geometries; the one sensitive rule fires on half the sound analyses too. Used as continuous scores the same statistics reach AUC 0.51 to 0.78, so this is a failure of thresholds rather than of the statistics. What no threshold repairs is that these diagnostics measure the prior's influence while the harm comes from the prior's location: with disconnected evidence and a tight prior four standard deviations from the truth, going from 100 to 400 per arm drops the warning rate from 0.98 to 0.01 while coverage stays near zero.
findings: Prespecified verdict: diagnostics fail at the thresholds the literature suggests. Composite sensitivity 0.366 (MCSE 0.002), false alarm 0.158; 0.127 and 0.025 outside the engineered positive controls.

Sensitivity and specificity trade off completely. Tight-and-loose prior refitting catches 0.83 of misses outside the controls and fires on 53% of covered replicates. Contraction, the prior-only benchmark and power-scaling keep false alarms low and catch almost nothing.

The composite adds almost nothing over its best component: 0.366 against contraction's 0.363, at a higher false-alarm rate. Requiring two of four rules to agree neither buys specificity nor recovers sensitivity.

More data makes the warning quieter while the answer stays wrong. Disconnected evidence, tight prior, true interaction four prior SDs away: coverage near zero at both sample sizes, warning rate 0.98 at 100 per arm and 0.01 at 400. Contraction is what every diagnostic reads as reassurance.

A first implementation measured power-scaling by posterior mean shift and found sensitivity 0.000 everywhere. That was our error: with a zero-centred prior, scaling the prior up and the likelihood down give identical posterior means, so the standard rule can never fire. Measured distributionally it works, and the verdict does not depend on the amendment.
The structural rank screen is the only rule with no false alarms at all, and it is blind to every failure where the contrast is estimable and the answer is still wrong.
CMU-02.not_answered: The other half of CMU-02, wiring these diagnostics into released software, is untouched; neither multinma nor cpaic is run. The model is conjugate Gaussian with an identity link, a correctly specified linear mean and known variances, so nothing transfers directly to a non-conjugate posterior where MCMC error enters and the diagnostics behave differently. Only automated thresholds are evaluated; a plot read by an experienced analyst is a different instrument. Thresholds were taken from the source literature and not tuned. CMP-14 is touched only for the generic aggregate-only interaction, not for component models, and IDN-06 is not addressed at all because this design contains no within-versus-between discrepancy.
CMU-02.design: A conjugate Gaussian population-adjusted network in which every piece of evidence reduces without loss to a normal observation, so the posterior and every power-scaled posterior are exact and no diagnostic is contaminated by MCMC noise. 120 scenarios crossing the evidence available about the weakly identified treatment, arm size, whether the truth agrees with the zero-centered prior, prior scale, and the target population. 2000 replicates each.
CMU-02.n_sim: 2000 per scenario, 240,000 datasets and 480,000 contrast evaluations
CMU-02.estimand: Target-population marginal C versus B mean difference, and the conditional interaction coefficient

DIA-03.title: Are the diagnostics reported alongside a population adjustment classifiers of its error?
DIA-03.question: Every population adjustment arrives with a panel of numbers beside it: effective sample size, the same figure as a percentage, the largest weight, standardized differences before and after adjustment, a distance between populations. A committee reads them as evidence about whether to believe the estimate, and a widely quoted rule says to worry below an effective sample size of about 30 to 35. Scored as classifiers of realized error, with discrimination and calibration, against known truth and under a declared distribution of analyses, what are they worth?
DIA-03.answer: They are variance statistics being read as bias warnings. Effective sample size separates the outcome-noise component of realized error at AUROC 0.847 and the transport component, which is the part covariate adjustment exists to remove, at 0.653. At the quoted cutoff of 35 it catches between a quarter and a third of material errors in every misspecification stratum, 0.309 where an effect modifier is omitted and the omission is diagnosable in principle, at specificity 0.926. Three of the panel's members are provably one statistic, since ESS/n = 1/(1+CV^2(w)) exactly and area under the ROC curve is invariant to monotone transformation; a fourth, the post-weighting balance on matched moments, is zero at the solution of the calibration equations and cannot discriminate anything. Across the cells where the rule stays silent, which is what an analyst acts on, the rate of material error runs from 0.045 to 0.835. On a decision-curve basis every rule in the panel is beaten by scrutinizing every analysis, up to an action threshold of 0.3.
findings: Prespecified verdict: the panel does not classify realized error at the thresholds in use. No rule reached sensitivity 0.80 with specificity 0.50 in every misspecification stratum. ESS below 35 reaches sensitivity 0.251 to 0.326 across strata at specificity 0.909 to 0.926.

The mechanism, which was registered before the run and holds: effective sample size discriminates the outcome-noise component at AUROC 0.847 and the transport component at 0.653, a gap of 0.194. It measures weight dispersion, and weight dispersion is a variance quantity.

The panel is smaller than it looks, by algebra rather than by simulation. ESS, ESS as a percentage and the coefficient of variation of the weights had identical areas under the ROC curve to 0.0e+00 within a fixed source size. The matched-moment balance statistic never exceeded 1.4e-14 and its apparent AUROC of 0.550 is discrimination of floating-point residual, not of balance.

Silence is where the damage is. Across the 88 cells the ESS rule never fires in, the material-error rate runs from 0.045 to 0.835. The registered version of this claim, a spread across the cells it does fire in, was not met (0.150 against a prespecified 0.30) because those cells are all bad; the complementary quantity is stronger and was not prespecified, so it is reported as an observation.

Decision-curve analysis: at action thresholds up to 0.3, flagging every analysis beats every rule in the panel. Only at 0.4 and above does a diagnostic earn its place, and it is the relative effective-sample-size rule rather than the absolute cutoff that gets quoted.

The same statistics work when they measure the actual gap. Pre-weighting imbalance predicts the unadjusted comparison's transport error at AUROC 0.891, against 0.655 for the same statistic applied to MAIC. These diagnostics are informative about the problem and uninformative about the solution: weighting sets to zero the very quantity they measure.

Our proposal, converting residual imbalance on a measured but unadjusted covariate into the units of the estimand with the source-estimated interaction, reaches 0.937 against the transport component in the diagnosable stratum where the best routine diagnostic reaches 0.851. That gain of 0.086 misses the 0.10 we registered, and is reported as a miss.

An adversarial critique of the design before the run found two arithmetic errors in the protocol: the dispersion factor was not the pure variance instrument it was described as wherever the cross-moment channel was on, and the target trial's variance was understated by a factor of two to three. Both were confirmed numerically and corrected before any result was seen.
DIA-03.not_answered: The second half of DIA-03 is untouched: no PSIS-LOO is computed at any hierarchical level and grouped study-level leave-one-out is no more implemented here than in the packages, so the mismatch between the level at which cross-validation is reported and the level at which the prediction is made remains open. DIA-06 is answered only in part; two estimator families and no adjustment are compared on identical replicates, but ML-NMR, NMI, doubly robust estimators and flexible learners are absent. The outcome is continuous with an identity link, which is what buys the exact error decomposition and is also the largest restriction: nothing here transfers to non-collapsible effect measures or time-to-event outcomes, where part of the error is a collapsibility artifact rather than an adjustment failure. Covariates are normal, comparisons are anchored, conditional constancy holds, and target moments are exact. The deployment weights are a declared judgment and nothing in this program measured them, which is why the primary results are within strata.
DIA-03.design: An anchored indirect comparison with a continuous outcome and an identity link, chosen so that the realized error of a linear estimator splits exactly into arm imbalance, transport error and outcome noise, and a covariate diagnostic can be scored against the only component it could possibly know about. 128 cells crossing an omitted effect modifier, a cross-moment modifier that no baseline table could reveal, overlap, source size, how correlated the omitted modifier is with the adjustment set, and a target dispersion ratio that destroys effective sample size while adding no bias where the modifier structure is correct. 4000 replicates per cell, four estimators. Primary results are reported within misspecification strata rather than over a mixture, so no investigator-chosen frequency enters the headline.
DIA-03.estimand: Transported A versus C mean difference in the target superpopulation; the anchored A versus B contrast as a secondary reference
methods_compared: MAIC matching means and standard deviations

MIS-03.title: What conditioning on sampled target moments costs
MIS-03.question: Population adjustment treats a target trial's published covariate means and standard deviations as exact, though they are sample estimates. By how much does that cost interval coverage at realistic sample sizes, and what would a publication have to report for a correction to work?
MIS-03.answer: Two things, established by different means. Analytically: the variance a standard interval omits is (1-2k)Var_T(tau)/n_T to first order, where k is how far the target trial's own treatment effect is modified by the same covariates as the source trial's, so the sign is set by a quantity the usual inputs do not identify; and a correction adding only the positive term is closer to the right variance than doing nothing only when k < 1/4. Empirically, and only in an exploratory subset: the omission runs from 9.5% too much variance to 14.9% too little and moves coverage between 92.1% and 96.2%. The registered analysis is uninformative and the confirmatory coverage question remains open.
findings: The prespecified analysis returned uninformative. Its gates require the reference interval and the negative controls to be nominal, and at poor overlap the Wald sandwich undercovers by up to 7 points for every method including scenarios with no effect modification at all, where the population omission is exactly zero. That is a source-variance failure, not a target-moment one.

The sign of the omission is an analytic identity, not a simulation finding: (1-2k)Var_T(tau)/n_T. Regressing the measured omission on it across all 216 scenarios with effect modification gives a slope of 1.003 (SE 0.042). An earlier draft claimed the simulation located the cancellation point; peer review corrected that and the claim was retracted.

The two corrections an analyst can deploy add only the positive term and omit the cross-covariance. They beat doing nothing only when k < 1/4, and are worse than doing nothing between 1/4 and 1/2. The design has no interior k with which to test this, so no recommendation is made for intermediate alignment. A draft claim that they help whenever k < 1/2 was wrong and was corrected in review.

In the exploratory subset the status quo was the only method to leave 93% to 97% coverage, and it left in both directions. Magnitude tracks the ratio of source to target information, so a large source trial matched to a small target publication is the worst case, not a small target trial.
Peer review left a standing recommendation of major revision. The confirmatory question needs a fresh registered run with an ex ante overlap restriction or a validated source variance estimator.
MIS-03.not_answered: The registered coverage question is not confirmatorily answered: every usable coverage result comes from a post-run restriction conditioning on an observed outcome. One estimator, one outcome type, one information structure. Covariates are multivariate normal, which is also the assumption the deployable correction is derived under, so it is measured under conditions favorable to it; skewed, bounded and categorical covariates are untested. The outcome is continuous and the effect additive, so marginal and conditional effects coincide, and nothing transfers directly to binary or time-to-event outcomes, where MAIC is most used. Effect modification lies exactly in the span of the matched moments, so this is a variance result under correct identification and says nothing about bias. The target moments and the target treatment effect come from the same trial, which is the common case but not the only one. STC, ML-NMR, ML-UMR and NMI have different sensitivities and are not covered. EST-07's other components, model uncertainty in reconstructed correlations, inclusion-criteria ambiguity and secular drift, are not sampling error and are untouched. The alignment parameter imposes exact non-negative proportionality between source and target modifier coefficients, so modifier sets differing in direction or overlapping only partially are untested.
MIS-03.design: Anchored MAIC on a continuous outcome, with the target trial's participants generated and then discarded so the estimator sees only a published baseline table. 252 scenarios crossing source size, target size, overlap, effect-modification strength calibrated to a fixed target-population standard deviation, the alignment between the two trials' effect modification, and whether the analyst's borrowed correlation is correct.
MIS-03.estimand: Target-superpopulation marginal A versus B mean difference, exact in closed form

The two corrections an analyst can deploy add only the positive term and omit the cross-covariance. They beat doing nothing only when k < 1/4, and are worse than doing nothing between 1/4 and 1/2. The design has no interior k with which to test this, so no recommendation is made for intermediate alignment. A draft claim that they help whenever k < 1/2 was wrong and was corrected in review.

In the exploratory subset the status quo was the only method to leave 93% to 97% coverage, and it left in both directions. Magnitude tracks the ratio of source to target information, so a large source trial matched to a small target publication is the worst case, not a small target trial.
Peer review left a standing recommendation of major revision. The confirmatory question needs a fresh registered run with an ex ante overlap restriction or a validated source variance estimator.
EST-07.not_answered: The registered coverage question is not confirmatorily answered: every usable coverage result comes from a post-run restriction conditioning on an observed outcome. One estimator, one outcome type, one information structure. Covariates are multivariate normal, which is also the assumption the deployable correction is derived under, so it is measured under conditions favorable to it; skewed, bounded and categorical covariates are untested. The outcome is continuous and the effect additive, so marginal and conditional effects coincide, and nothing transfers directly to binary or time-to-event outcomes, where MAIC is most used. Effect modification lies exactly in the span of the matched moments, so this is a variance result under correct identification and says nothing about bias. The target moments and the target treatment effect come from the same trial, which is the common case but not the only one. STC, ML-NMR, ML-UMR and NMI have different sensitivities and are not covered. EST-07's other components, model uncertainty in reconstructed correlations, inclusion-criteria ambiguity and secular drift, are not sampling error and are untouched. The alignment parameter imposes exact non-negative proportionality between source and target modifier coefficients, so modifier sets differing in direction or overlapping only partially are untested.
EST-07.design: Anchored MAIC on a continuous outcome, with the target trial's participants generated and then discarded so the estimator sees only a published baseline table. 252 scenarios crossing source size, target size, overlap, effect-modification strength calibrated to a fixed target-population standard deviation, the alignment between the two trials' effect modification, and whether the analyst's borrowed correlation is correct.
EST-07.estimand: Target-superpopulation marginal A versus B mean difference, exact in closed form
